comment: The Phase-9b pilot list (docs/national-scaleout.md §7). Kept in the repo so the
batch is reproducible and the selection is auditable: `.claude/workflows/pilot-batch.mjs`
Naming honesty: KMR names only 292 of the 1,304 registered fornborgar. Where the
register carries a `lamningsnamn` it is used verbatim; where it does not, the site
is identified by its lämningsnummer and nothing else. The doc's §1 guesses at which
record is Torsburgen and which is Halleberg are marked [reported] there and stay
[reported] here — the register does not say, and the pilot does not pretend it does.
1. all three `large`-preset outliers (the only sites over 1 km);
2. Broborg, the reference site every earlier phase was built against;
3. the §7 famous forts that KMR actually names;
4. the largest named fort in each remaining county, east-coast first, so the
water path (§4.3) is exercised across the whole uplift gradient;
5. one non-polygon site, because 43 of 1,304 have no extent polygon and their
rampart derivation must skip rather than fail.

sites.why: large preset, 5.9 km — the biggest registered extent in Sweden (Vänersnäs/Västra Tunhem; plausibly the Halleberg plateau [reported])
large preset, 1.4 km — the biggest on Gotland (plausibly Torsburgen [reported])
large preset, 1.5 km — Ramundersborg, and KMR names it
Broborg — the reference site, rebuilt under v1.5 to compare against the Phase-8 bundle
Ismantorps fornborg — the §7 list, named in KMR
Eketorps borg — the §7 list, named in KMR
Gråborg — the §7 list, named in KMR
Runsa borg — the §7 list, named in KMR
Garnisonen, Adelsö — the Birka garrison. KMR names no record 'Birka borg', so the pilot takes the Birka-area fortification the register does name
Skansberget, Adelsö — the second named fort in Birka's parish
Vikingaberget, Ekerö — Mälaren archipelago, heavy water path
the larger of Järfälla's two forts (the §7 list wants Gåseborg, which is in this parish; KMR names neither, so this is not claimed to be it)
Predikstolen — largest named fort in Uppsala, 478 m
Borgen — largest named fort in Stockholm county
Jättunaskansen — largest named fort in Södermanland, the densest county
Borgberget — largest named fort in Kalmar
Slottet — largest named fort on Gotland, a second Baltic site
Bolströ borg — largest named fort in Västmanland
Borgberget — Gävleborg, the northern end of the east-coast water counties
Borgen — Västernorrland, the northernmost water county in §1
Träleborg — largest named fort in Västra Götaland, the Vänern side
Borren — Skåne, an inland/southern site with no paleo-shoreline in range
Silverberget — Blekinge, south coast
Kungsbjär — Halland, west coast (a different uplift regime from the Baltic sites)
Skansen — Värmland, one of the 39 sites whose far rings reach the Norwegian border (the Copernicus case, §2b)
Tarsta berg — Örebro, fully inland: the no-water path
Borg — line geometry, no extent polygon: the rampart derivation must skip cleanly (43 of 1,304 sites are like this)
